factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A diode is a circuit element that allows electric current to flow in only one direction.

factualClaims.subject: Zener
factualClaims.sourceRef: Engineering LibreTexts, Introduction to Physical Electronics (Wilson), §1.10 "Reverse Biased/Breakdown"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A Zener diode is a reverse-biased diode designed to operate in breakdown, used as a voltage reference.

factualClaims.subject: LED
factualClaims.sourceRef: Engineering LibreTexts, Semiconductors, "Light Emitting Diodes"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: An LED is a p-n junction semiconductor device that emits light (a photon) when forward biased, due to electron-hole recombination.

factualClaims.subject: thermistors
factualClaims.sourceRef: Physics LibreTexts, Electricity and Magnetism (Tatum), §4.3 "Resistance and Temperature"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A thermistor is a semiconducting device whose resistance is very sensitive to temperature.

factualClaims.subject: transistors
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 3, §9.7 "Semiconductor Devices"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A transistor is a device that can amplify or switch electrical signals.

factualClaims.subject: gears
factualClaims.sourceRef: Engineering LibreTexts, Mechanics Map (Moore et al.), §11.2 "Belt- and Gear-Driven Systems"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Meshed gear teeth have equal speed at the point of contact; gear ratio = radius(output)/radius(input) = teeth(output)/teeth(input).

factualClaims.subject: gears
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, §9.5 "Simple Machines"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Mechanical advantage (MA) is the ratio of output to input force magnitudes for a simple machine.

factualClaims.subject: pulleys
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, §9.5 "Simple Machines"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: An ordinary (single) pulley has MA of 1, changing only the direction of a force, not its magnitude; multi-cable pulley systems' MA approximates the number of supporting cables.

factualClaims.subject: pulleys
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, §9.5 "Simple Machines"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Mechanical advantage (MA) is the ratio of output to input force magnitudes for a simple machine.

factualClaims.subject: lever class I
factualClaims.sourceRef: Physics LibreTexts, Body Physics (Davis), §6.2 "Body Levers"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: First-class levers have the fulcrum in the middle, between the load and resistance/effort.

factualClaims.subject: lever class II
factualClaims.sourceRef: Physics LibreTexts, Body Physics (Davis), §6.2 "Body Levers"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Second-class levers have the resistance/load in the middle, between the fulcrum and effort.

factualClaims.subject: lever class III
factualClaims.sourceRef: Physics LibreTexts, Body Physics (Davis), §6.2 "Body Levers"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Third-class levers have the effort in the middle, between the fulcrum and load.

factualClaims.subject: force
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, Physics, §4.3 "Newton's Second Law of Motion"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Force relates to mass and acceleration via Newton's second law (the same relationship, F=ma, underlying the weight formula W=mg already sourced for AC3.1).

factualClaims.subject: inter-relationships between force, work, energy, power and efficiency
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, §7.7 "Power"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: P = W/t (equation 7.69); SI unit watt, 1 W = 1 J/s

factualClaims.subject: current (calculation, D.C. circuits)
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §9.3 "Resistivity and Resistance"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: R = V/I (equation 9.8)

factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §9.3 "Resistivity and Resistance"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: R = V/I (equation 9.8)

factualClaims.subject: values of power in parallel and series D.C. circuits
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §9.5 "Electrical Energy and Power"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: P = I^2 R = V^2/R (equation 9.13) -- resistive/thermal power dissipated by a resistor.

factualClaims.subject: voltage drop
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §9.3 "Resistivity and Resistance"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: R = V/I (equation 9.8)

factualClaims.subject: capacitors
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §8.1 "Capacitors and Capacitance"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A capacitor is a device used to store electrical charge and electrical energy.

factualClaims.subject: rectifiers
factualClaims.sourceRef: Engineering LibreTexts, Semiconductor Devices -- Theory and Application (Fiore), §3.2 "Rectification"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: Rectification is the process of turning an alternating-current waveform into a direct-current waveform (a signal with only a single polarity).

factualClaims.subject: diacs
factualClaims.sourceRef: Workforce LibreTexts, Electric Circuits III -- Semiconductors (Kuphaldt), §7.4 "The DIAC"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A DIAC is formed by joining two Shockley diodes in parallel facing opposite directions, giving bidirectional (AC) triggering.

factualClaims.subject: triacs
factualClaims.sourceRef: Workforce LibreTexts, Electric Circuits III -- Semiconductors (Kuphaldt), §7.6 "The TRIAC"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A TRIAC acts like two SCRs connected back-to-back for bidirectional (AC) operation.

factualClaims.subject: thyristors
factualClaims.sourceRef: Workforce LibreTexts, Electric Circuits III -- Semiconductors (Kuphaldt), §7.5 "The Silicon-Controlled Rectifier (SCR)"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: An SCR/thyristor is a latching semiconductor switch: once triggered on, internal feedback keeps it conducting until current is reduced to cutoff (a hysteretic device that, triggered during an AC half-cycle, remains on until current decreases to zero).

factualClaims.subject: instrument for measuring resistance
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §10.4 "Electrical Measuring Instruments"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: An ohmmeter measures resistance, computed via Ohm's law (R=V/I) from a known/measured voltage and current.

factualClaims.subject: instrument for measuring current
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §10.4 "Electrical Measuring Instruments"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: An ammeter measures current and is connected in series with the device/component being measured.

factualClaims.subject: instrument for measuring voltage
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §10.4 "Electrical Measuring Instruments"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A voltmeter measures voltage/potential difference and is connected in parallel with the device being measured.

factualClaims.subject: production of a magnetic field
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, College Physics 2e, §22.9 "Magnetic Fields Produced by Currents: Ampere's Law"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field (circular loops around the wire); direction given by the right-hand rule (thumb in direction of current, fingers curl in direction of the field).

factualClaims.subject: single-loop generator
factualClaims.sourceRef: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 2, §13.1 "Faraday's Law"
factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: epsilon = -N dPhi/dt (equation 13.2) -- induced EMF equals the negative rate of change of magnetic flux.

factualClaims.subject: sine-wave (AC generation principle)

factualClaims.normalizedClaimValue: An AC voltage waveform is described by V = V0 sin(2*pi*f*t) (equation 20.38), where f is the frequency in hertz.
